nodes.name: 02:30 IST daily
nodes.notes: GENERIC_TIMEZONE is Asia/Kolkata (set in the Dockerfile), so this cron is IST, not UTC. NOTE: this trigger does not itself run the recompute — see the next node's notes.

parameters.query:
-- The recompute itself is a NODE.JS script (scripts/recompute-scores.mjs,
-- run via `npm run score`), not SQL -- there is no recompute_all_scores()
-- function for this node to call, and an earlier version of this workflow
-- wrongly suggested one. A single Postgres node cannot invoke it.
--
-- So this checks COVERAGE (how many customers currently have a score), not
-- FRESHNESS (whether a recompute ran recently) -- there is deliberately no
-- `where computed_at > ...` filter. An earlier version had one, and on any
-- machine where `npm run score` had not been run in the last 24h it read
-- zero rows and false-failed every single time, which is exactly what it did
-- on first use here.
select count(*) as scored,
       max(computed_at) as computed_at
from v_customer_scores;

nodes.name: Score coverage check
nodes.notes: Read-only, against the agent role. To make this workflow actually TRIGGER a recompute (not just check one happened), add an Execute Command node running `npm run score` against a mounted copy of the repo, or an HTTP node calling a new endpoint that wraps scripts/recompute-scores.mjs -- neither exists yet.

nodes.name: Fewer scored than expected?
nodes.notes: ~800 customers have a score in a healthy state. Under 700 means coverage has dropped — a customer table grew without a matching recompute, or scoring silently failed for a chunk of them — worth knowing before the morning outreach in workflow 03 reads incomplete scores. leftValue wraps $json.scored in Number(...) because Postgres count(*) is a bigint, and the pg driver returns bigints as STRINGS (avoids silent precision loss past 2^53) — comparing that string directly against a number literal fails with "Wrong type: '801' is a string but was expecting a number", regardless of the node's typeValidation setting.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ok: true, scored: $json.scored, computed_at: $json.computed_at } }];
